name: HumanTouch
description: AI edits your writing. It stays recognizably yours.

paragraphs: AI editors tend to pull every writer toward the same voice. Ask one to tidy a paragraph and it regenerates the whole thing: fragments become full sentences, "I think" becomes "it is clear that", the odd phrase that was the point of the paragraph is gone, and nothing tells you it happened.

HumanTouch is an authorial-preservation layer. It lets a model change your writing while keeping the boundary visible: the model may change expression; it may not silently change meaning, certainty, facts or the habits that make the writing yours.
It does not try to make text sound "human". People write differently; there is no one human voice to aim at. It tries to keep text sounding like its author.
features: Observed (measured on the Space, no model): rhythm, sentence structure, vocabulary, punctuation, certainty.
Inferred (simple proxies over those measurements, capped at moderate confidence): directness, formality, warmth, expressiveness.

Model judgment (optional Groq call): abstraction, humor, imagery, plus things it notices. Every such claim must quote your samples exactly or it is dropped and counted. If the call fails, those dimensions read "not…
Signature patterns (repeated phrases, openers, punctuation habits), "your writing tends to…" statements, and sample-quality advice (it says when a sample is too small or too uniform).
Contextual voice: tag samples as Everyday, Professional, Academic, Poetic or Social; with two or more contexts it separates habits that are stable from those that change with context.

requirements.text: HumanTouch has no database, no accounts and no analytics of its own.
